hero.heading: WordPress development your editors can live with.
hero.subtitle: Themes, custom blocks, and WooCommerce when a store belongs in WordPress. The goal is a site the team can update on a Tuesday.

overview: WordPress is the right tool when content editors are the main users. I build or repair the theme, the fields, and the checkout so publishing does not require a developer for every sentence.
problem: A theme from a marketplace looks complete until you try to change a section. Then every edit is a shortcode, a plugin conflict, or a broken layout.
solution: I use a small set of blocks and fields that match the real pages, keep plugins to the ones you need, and make the editor preview close to the live page.

faqs.question: Can you work on a site that is already live?
faqs.answer: Yes. Changes happen on a staging copy. The live site moves when the new templates are ready.

faqs.question: Do you support WooCommerce payments?
faqs.answer: Yes, including gateways such as Stripe. The payment setup is part of the scope when the store needs it.
